Soy and Prostate Cancer
The role of soy phytoestrogens in prostate cancer is also controversial.31,32 While 
estrogen is used to treat established cases of prostate cancer because it inhibits cancer 
growth, estrogens have also been associated with the development of benign prostatic 
hyperplasia and prostate cancer.33 Over the last 30 years, studies have shown 
­conflicting results regarding the impact of soy on prostate cancer. Men who ­consumed 
a soy-enriched diet have lower prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels compared with 
controls. One study demonstrated that adding 2 oz of soy grits per day to the diets of
